summary: Iteration 15 — validated P3 enhancements: (a) GET /api/dashboard/my-sv-weekly endpoint with month/engineer_id params; (b) frontend MySvWeeklyChart card on SiteVisitsPage with month picker that refetches on change; (c) engineer_name field on new visit form auto-populated with logged-in username; (d) watermarked photo upload burning engineer+timestamp badge into the saved JPEG. All 9 new pytests pass and all 46 prior pytests still pass. Frontend visual + programmatic checks confirm chart shape, month dropdown re-fetch, engineer auto-fill, and watermark presence in the saved file.

issues: Recharts emits initial 'width(-1) height(-1)' warnings before container measures; chart renders correctly after first paint — purely a console noise, no user impact.

React hydration warning observed in console: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' — likely from a non-string child inside <option> in MySvWeeklyChart's <select>. Not blocking but should be cleaned.

action_items: Cosmetic: clean up the <option> child in MySvWeeklyChart month dropdown so React stops emitting hydration warning ('<span> cannot be a child of <option>').
Cosmetic: silence the initial recharts 'width(-1) height(-1)' warnings by giving ResponsiveContainer an explicit minHeight or by waiting one layout tick before rendering the chart.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend endpoint correctly enforces that engineers cannot pass engineer_id to inspect another user's chart (target_user_id stays as themselves) — verified by test_engineer_engineer_id_param_is_ignored.
Date bucketing (day 1-7→W1, 8-14→W2, 15-21→W3, 22-28→W4, 29-31→W5) verified end-to-end with seeded April 2026 visits on day 3, 10, 25.
by_project is sorted DESC and capped at 8 entries — verified.
Invalid month formats ('2026', 'foo', '2026-13-01', 'abcd-ef') return 400 with the canonical 'month must be YYYY-MM' detail.
Frontend engineer_name on the new visit form has data-testid='input-engineer-name' and pre-fills with user.username — verified value='rutvij0213' immediately after page load.

Watermark is burned into the saved file on disk (not just the DOM thumbnail) — confirmed via PIL: bottom-right 280x80 ROI of a fresh 1024x768 solid-orange JPEG shows 33.77% dark pixels (luminance<100) vs 0% in the top-left baseline, and avg R drops 199→155 in that ROI — proving the dark-green badge with white text was rasterized into the JPEG before upload.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (chart + month-change + engineer autopop + watermark all verified)

To rerun watermark validation, generate /tmp/test_upload.jpg with PIL (1024x768 solid orange) then upload via [data-testid=input-photo-file] and inspect bottom-right 280x80 ROI of the newest /app/backend/uploads/site-visits/*.jpg — expect >30% dark pixels (luminance<100). The strict RGB-tolerance check from the review request (target (10,46,31) tol 40) does NOT work because the badge uses alpha=0.7 over the underlying image; use luminance-based detection instead.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. The two console warnings (recharts dimensions + <span> in <option>) are cosmetic React/library noise and don't affect functionality.
